result:
I found 10 rules whose code didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. I then ran a check script that reads each of the 150 docstrings, computes the expected price, and compares it with the actual function over a range of quantities and unit prices. All 150 now match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 16, 92 | The price was capped instead of the discount (`min(base, cap) * pct`) | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 11 | Used `qty > 50`, so exactly 50 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 50` |
| 19, 30, 80, 131 | Used `round()`, which rounds instead of flooring to the won | Changed to integer floor division `//` |
| 77 | Marked as marginal but discounted the whole amount | Changed to `(qty - 10) * unit * 12 // 100` |
| 82 | Only applied the cap when the discount exceeded 200,000 | Cap now always applies via `min(disc, 100000)` |

Rules 47 (`qty >= 101`) and 72 (`qty > 20`) are written differently from their docstrings, but at the threshold quantity the marginal discount is 0 either way. They give the same results, so I left them unchanged.

STATUS: DONE
